novelty_flags.label: prop:sanity-chen-reduction and all repeated Chen anchors
novelty_flags.one_line: The cited arXiv v1 does contain the LP A_x w_x=β_x and full-column-rank point-identification result, but it is Eq. (2) and Proposition 3.6 in §3.2.2, not “Proposition 4, pp. 8--12” as repeatedly claimed.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: oeq:hausdorff-frontier
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: The claimed rate question is conditional on the maintained uniform local fiber-Hölder modulus (C,ν), including its stated cross-stratum extension; that modulus is not derived by this proposal.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: Sharp uniform Hausdorff-rate result only on the declared class P_{J,δ,γ,C,ν}; this conditional regularity framing supports at most the assessed field tier.

source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The source defines A_x=[α_x(f,y)] and β_x, gives the LP A_x w_x=β_x in Eq. (2), and states point identification when A_x has full column rank in Proposition 3.6.

The paper assumes no future dependence conditional on current state, action, and reward; uses S_{t+1} as a shadow variable; and identifies value through bridge existence/uniqueness and completeness in an augmented MDP.
The paper studies monotone nonignorable missingness, proposes an inverse-probability-weighted value estimator, and supplies statistical inference.
The paper extends robust finite- and infinite-horizon dynamic-programming results when the ambiguity set has a rectangularity property.
The paper reduces discrete causal questions to polynomial programming problems and develops automated certified numerical causal bounds using dual relaxation and spatial branch-and-bound.
The paper constructs confidence sets for full identified sets and subvectors in nonlinear likelihood or moment-(in)equality models.
The paper gives bootstrap calibrated-projection intervals with uniform asymptotic coverage for scalar components and smooth functions of partially identified parameters.
The paper studies semiparametric efficiency for OPE in Markov decision processes and develops doubly robust, cross-fit evaluation methods.
The paper gives conditions under which a continuous linear functional is strongly identified and root-n estimable despite weakly identified nuisance functions.
The paper establishes a necessary-and-sufficient identifying condition for a static MNAR mean functional with a shadow variable without identifying the full data law.
The paper studies proximal counterfactual-mean identification and inference when bridge solutions need not be unique.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Correct every Chen citation to the pinned v1 locator—§3.2.2, Eq. (2), Proposition 3.6—and state explicitly that S_{t+1} plays Chen’s always-observed F role in the H=1 reduction.

Make the strict-containment deliverable concrete by giving the exact H=2 binary-action/three-reward rational parameterization and the promised observable minors before attempting a general sign elimination.

For the Hausdorff branch, either derive a modulus from explicit semialgebraic degree/stratum data or define the confidence image after intersection with the declared compatible stratum class and prove that unrestricted-fiber leakage is negligible.

recommended_next_step: Revise the Chen locator and sharpen the conditional Hausdorff branch; then advance the dynamic face-pasting/strict-containment angle to Stage 0.
